info.title: Luma API
info.description: Read cases, evidence, proposals, execution and audit history. Make permitted decisions and follow authenticated progress streams. Manage organizations, memberships and installed connections. Organization endpoints require a session cookie.

get.summary: Read supported governed action mappings for this record type
Read governed actions available on a saved view

post.summary: Review each proposed record change before acting
Propose separately governed commands for selected records
post.description: Rechecks current authorization and the reviewed change. Commands retain owner policy, approval, idempotency and independent verification. Each selected record returns its own result.

get.description: Read policy-bound custom field proposals your role may see. Filter by the affected record to show its waiting proposals.
Read the exact before and proposed typed values, policy decision, expiry and current revisions before responding.

post.summary: Approve or reject a workflow field change
post.description: Respond to the reviewed policy decision. Stale field or value revisions and mismatched review fingerprints are refused. Approval grants only this immutable proposal; the worker rechecks permission and policy before writing.

get.description: Read fields that your role may see for this record type. Archived fields are excluded unless requested.

post.description: Create a typed Luma field with German and English labels and permission gates from the catalog. Repeat the same commandId to recover its result.

put.description: Change labels, permissions and choices using the current revision. Changing type or removing choices is refused while values exist.

post.description: Make an archived Luma field visible again with its existing values and history. Provider-observed fields cannot be restored through this command.
Hide a field from active record views while retaining values and change history.

post.summary: Read custom field values of several records
post.description: Reads permitted fields and their values for up to 100 records of one type, as list columns show them. Records you cannot see return no values; records without values are absent.

get.description: Read permitted fields and their values on a record you can access. Provider-observed fields remain read-only.

put.description: Atomically change typed Luma-owned values and record who changed each field. Use revision 0 for an unset field or its current value revision. Stale changes are refused; null clears a field.

post.description: Filter, sort and group supported records by fields your role can see. Predicates run before pagination; returns record identities for domain detail views. Group counts include unset values and are capped at 100 groups.

get.description: Read the latest 100 immutable definition changes, or value changes for one record, with actor identity and timestamps.

get.summary: Read operational packages and installed workspace configuration

post.summary: Review package additions and missing requirements
Install reviewed package definitions without activating workflows or granting access
Remove package definitions while retaining business records and audit history

get.description: Lists live views you own or that are shared with you, and the built-in views your role can read. Queries are returned in format 2; views stored in format 1 are upgraded on read.

post.description: Accepts a query in format 2, or format 1 for compatibility, and stores it in format 2. Conditions, sorting and grouping must use the list catalog; unknown columns are kept and shown as unavailable. Repeating a command with the same content returns the saved view.

get.description: Returns the view with its query in format 2. A condition, sort or grouping that no longer matches the list needs repair before the view can be previewed.

put.description: Accepts a query in format 2 or 1 and stores a new revision in format 2. A stale `expectedRevision` is refused with 409.

post.summary: Copy a saved query to a private view
post.description: Copies the query in format 2. Actions you cannot invoke are left out of the copy.

get.description: Returns up to 100 revisions, newest first. Revisions stored in format 1 are upgraded to format 2 on read.

post.description: Runs a query in format 2 or 1 through the record owners. Rows are keyed by the list catalog's column IDs. Incomplete evidence and unavailable columns are reported explicitly; a condition the list cannot yet run is refused with 422. No action executes.

post.summary: Draft a view from a description
post.description: Proposes a constrained query in format 2 and its preview. Saving requires explicit review. Ambiguous identities and unsupported requests need clarification.

get.description: Returns what you last had open on a list page in this workspace: the view, unsaved changes, your default view, view order and personal display settings. `state` is null until you change something on the page. Requires read access to the list.

put.description: Replaces your state for one list page. Send a `sequence` higher than the last one this client sent; a save with a lower or equal sequence than the stored one is ignored and the stored state is returned. Search text and page position are not part of the state. Read-only support views cannot save.

delete.summary: Reset a list page to its default
delete.description: Removes your remembered state and personal display settings for one list page. The page then opens your default view, or the built-in default.

post.description: Exports the visible columns of a list query as CSV, reading the same records the list shows. Needs permission to export lists and to read the list; read-only support views cannot export. At most 5,000 rows are exported; `truncated` says when the list has more, and the file ends with the `@truncated` label. Send column headings in `labels`, keyed by column ID. Every export is recorded in the audit log without its values.

delete.description: Removes your remembered state and personal display settings for every list page in this workspace. Saved views are not changed.

get.summary: List available apps and workspace installations
get.description: Includes the permissions each app declares, the access it requests, the scopes granted to each installation and roles that hold its permissions.

post.summary: Install an app in this workspace
post.description: Requires `apps.manage` and every scope the app requests: you can only grant access you have. Send the requested scopes you reviewed; a changed request returns 409. Use null for a first installation or the current version to reinstall. Reinstalling restores no role permissions.

post.summary: Approve access an upgraded app requests
post.description: Requires `apps.manage` and each approved scope. Until approved, the app keeps working with the scopes granted earlier.

Requires `apps.manage`. Stops new app operations, deletes connection credentials and scope grants, and removes the app’s permissions from every role. Historical records remain. Requests already dispatched may finish.

post.summary: Read stock protection settings and incidents
Configure stock protection for one store
post.description: Enabling preauthorizes bounded incident holds and releases. Send the last read revision. Disabling active holds requires release or keep until recovery.

post.summary: Release, extend or approve stock protection

get.summary: Check whether you can ask Luma here
get.description: Any member can check this. Asking Luma needs the Use Ask Luma permission and a regional model route with zero data retention. Without either, `available` is false and `reason` explains what is missing. `reads` lists the records the assistant can look up for you, based on your role. `contextual` reports whether record and chart assistance is available in this workspace.

post.summary: Ask a question about your workspace
post.description: Answers a question from the orders, issues, stock, fulfillment, customer profiles and returns you can see in this workspace. Luma reads current records for every question, with your access, and never changes anything. Citation markers in `content` link to the records the answer used, with their source and observation time. Send earlier turns in `history` for follow-up questions; Luma does not store conversations. Optional context rereads a selected record or exact chart filters before answering; it requires contextual assistance to be enabled for this workspace. Each answer is limited in reads, length and time; when a limit is reached, `outcome` is `incomplete`. Returns 503 with a reason when the assistant is unavailable here or the model fails, times out or returns nothing usable.

timeZone.description: Calendar days and weeks are counted in this time zone.

connectionId.description: Count only records reported by this connection. Charts of Luma records ignore it.

point.description: A point key from the chart, or `previous` for a timeline’s previous stretch. Omit to list every point.

series.description: A series ID from the chart. Omit to list every series.

asOf.description: The chart’s evaluation time, at most 15 minutes old, so time-based rules classify records the same way. Defaults to now.

get.description: Lists connection-pair rules for SKU codes and ERP order references to Shopify orders, with their last check, total links and any reason they are waiting or blocked.

put.description: Requires Manage imports. Creates a rule with revision zero, or enables or disables an existing rule using its current revision. Each save is audited and enabled rules run with the caller’s current access. Disabling stops future links and keeps existing links. SKU rules require unique normalized codes and compatible units; order rules match an ERP order’s explicit external order number, as JTL and Cin7 report it, to one selected Shopify store. Every application rechecks current evidence and preserves mapping history.

post.description: Requires Manage imports. Shows counts and up to 20 examples for the selected record type and connections. Does not link records. Duplicate codes or references, conflicting mappings or units, manually separated records and stale or missing evidence are skipped.

get.description: Shows, for each connection and record type, whether Luma is importing history, keeping records in sync, retrying or waiting for someone. Includes imported record counts, the creation-date range Luma holds, any source history limit, the last successful sync and recent runs. A record type is `not_requested` when the connection does not include it and `not_granted` when the source did not grant it.

Lists one sync’s runs, newest first, 20 per page: history imports, change syncs and full checks, what started each, and how many records were imported, unchanged, waiting, not imported or no longer found. A running run shows its progress so far. Pass `nextCursor` as `before` for older runs.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `before` for older runs; null on the last page.

get.description: Lists one sync’s source records in one state, 25 per page in source key order: `pending` records wait for a record they depend on, `failed` records could not be imported and `missing` records were imported before but recent full checks no longer found them. Each shows its source ID, the reason when Luma knows it, and the Luma record it was imported as. Pass `nextCursor` as `cursor` for the next page; a cursor from another request returns 422.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

post.description: Requires `sync.manage`. Pauses or resumes a sync, retries now, requests a full check against the source (`reconcile`) or imports the history again (`reimport`). Resuming, retrying and re-importing continue with the caller’s access. Re-importing keeps every imported record; unchanged records are recognized and not duplicated. Commands are idempotent.

Requires `sync.manage`. Applies one command to every sync of a connection it changes, together: `pause` pauses running syncs, `resume` resumes paused syncs and syncs whose person lost access, and `retry` syncs every sync that is neither paused nor blocked now. Resuming and retrying continue with the caller’s access. Returns how many syncs changed and the connection’s updated state. Commands are idempotent.

get.description: Lists the source records that represent one SKU, location, order or order line, how each was linked, and possible matches in other sources. Suggestions share a SKU code or an ERP order’s marketplace order reference. Configured automatic linking rules may apply unambiguous matches; other suggestions require review. Order-line choices are current lines in other sources of an already-linked order, with the same units. Descriptions and SKU text never establish line identity.

post.description: Requires `sync.manage`. Confirms that another SKU, location, order or order line is the same record (`link`), or separates one connection’s source from it (`unlink`). Luma applies the change in the background, keeps the previous mapping as history and re-projects affected projections. Order links keep each source’s lines and shipments separate and preserve old references. Line links require a shared parent order and equal quantity units, and survive later source reads. Poll the returned request for its outcome.

get.description: Returns whether a link or unlink request is waiting, running, completed or failed, with an explanation when it failed.

post.description: Requires `connections.manage`. The connection remains pending until a successful permission check.

patch.description: Owners may impose observe-only or restore workspace inheritance. A connection cannot enable writes in an observe-only workspace.

post.description: Replaces credentials and clears verified permissions. Check the connection again to restore access. Also reconnects a connection whose provider revoked access, keeping its ID, mappings and history; a disconnected connection returns 409. Use the latest connection version.
Deletes stored credentials and stops further use. Does not revoke provider tokens or cancel requests already sent. Install a new connection to reconnect.

get.description: Browse provider names and categories. Filter by storefront or ERP.
Look up a provider by its ID. Returns 404 if the provider is not in the catalog.
Returns the authoritative connection for each order and inventory fact group. Unknown or conflicting authority cannot authorize a correction.

post.description: Overrides one fact group or restores its category default with a null connectionId. Requires workspace settings permission, the current revision and a stable commandId for retries. Each change records its actor and before/after override without changing source evidence.

get.description: Returns the latest 100 changes, newest first, including the actor and previous and new overrides.
Separates simulator proof, reviewed workspace live declarations and unknown sources. Changed source or credential revisions invalidate a declaration.

post.description: Reads one purchase-order page through the authenticated connection and retains source identity evidence without record payloads. The review expires in five minutes. Simulator sources cannot be declared live.

post.summary: Declare live operational use or revoke it
post.description: An authorized person confirms live operational use with a reason and a fresh exact-source review. This is a reviewed workspace declaration, not provider certification. Retry-safe commands retain actor, revision and evidence; previous history never changes classification.

post.summary: Assign or clear a case owner
post.description: Changes responsibility with an optimistic revision. Assignment is audited and grants no approval or execution authority.

get.description: List issues that need a person, active work or history. `where` takes conditions on the issues catalog fields, such as class, state, owner, source, attention reason, freshness, diagnosis, resolution, record type and dates; `q` searches summaries and records. Results sort by urgency by default: severity, then the oldest attention request or detection, then ID. `group` returns each group’s count and first rows. Freshness is fresh only while the investigation’s evidence is still valid; stale and unknown evidence are never reported as fresh. Use the returned cursor with the same query. Refresh from the first page as cases change.

schema.description: Issues of one owner, or `unassigned`. Kept for older links; prefer an `owner` condition.
Matches the summary, the record ID or its type, ignoring case. Never stored in saved views.
JSON-encoded conditions: `{"match":"all"|"any","conditions":[{"field","op","value","source"}]}`. Fields and operators follow the list catalog; unsupported combinations return 400.
Group rows by a field, such as `status` or `placed:week`. Each group returns its count and its first rows.
JSON-encoded group key from `groups[].key`, such as `"open"`, `true` or `null`, to read more rows of one group. Requires `group`.
Rows returned per group, from 1 to 50.
Days, weeks and months in conditions such as `today` or `within_last`, and date groups, follow this time zone.

`urgency` puts high severity first, then the oldest attention request, or the oldest detection for issues that need nobody. `waitingSince` is when the issue started waiting on a person; issues that wait on nobody come last in both directions.
Defaults to ascending for `urgency` and `waitingSince`, descending for `detected` and `lastActivity`.

groups.description: With `group`: each group in display order with its exact count and first rows, whose issues are in `items`. With `groupKey`: the one group, with this page of its rows. An issue with several sources counts in each source’s group.

groupsTruncated.description: More than 50 groups match; narrow the conditions to see the rest.

get.description: Returns persisted observation and verification references ordered by immutable ID, including evidence outside the current diagnosis. Pages default to 25 references and allow at most 100. Reuse cursors only for the same organization, case and page size. As evidence arrives, refresh from the first page and deduplicate by ID. Completeness is unknown unless explicitly recorded for the observation. A null source update time means unknown, regardless of observation freshness.

Returns the current persisted investigation and up to 100 evidence references. Use the evidence endpoint to read further historical references. Recommendations require review; they do not authorize execution. Unavailable cases return not found.

get.summary: Read the Luma support view in this browser
get.description: Returns the read-only support view this browser holds: the workspace, the member it shows and when it ends. Inactive when there is none or it ended, with the reason it just ended.

post.description: Exchanges the single-use token from a staff console link, within two minutes, for a support view cookie. While the cookie is present, workspace routes show the viewed member’s access read-only and refuse every change.
Ends the support view this browser holds, records its end and clears its cookie.

get.description: Returns sign-ins, failed sign-in attempts and security changes for your own account, newest first, 20 per page. Events are kept for one year; IP addresses and devices for 90 days.

get.summary: List Luma support requests for your account
get.description: Returns requests from Luma support to inspect your account, and approved inspections that are still open, newest first. Inspection shows your workspaces and roles, sign-in factor status, active sessions and security activity; it never shows passwords or factor secrets.

post.summary: Approve or decline a Luma support request for your account
post.description: Approving lets the support team member who asked inspect your account for thirty minutes from now. Repeating the same answer returns the current list; a request that lapsed or got another answer returns 409.

post.summary: End an approved Luma support inspection of your account
post.description: Ends approved access now; the support team’s next read is refused. Emergency access can’t be revoked. Revoking again returns the current list; access that already ended returns 409.

put.description: Stores the interface language Luma uses for email to you, such as invitations, notifications and account notices. The web app calls this after you pick a language.

get.description: Includes workspaces where your membership is suspended. Their `membershipStatus` is `suspended`, and their tenant routes return 403 until the membership is reactivated.

post.description: Creates a workspace in this cell’s confirmed data region with you as its owner. Other regions are rejected.

get.description: Returns your membership, role and effective permissions. Changes to your role apply on the next request.

patch.description: Requires `members.manage`. Only owners change ownership; others can only assign roles, and change members, whose permissions they hold. The last active owner cannot be demoted.

delete.description: The last active owner cannot be removed or demoted.

get.summary: List workspace roles and the permissions they can grant
get.description: Returns built-in and custom roles with member counts, and the permission catalog including permissions declared by installed apps. Any member can read roles.

post.description: Requires `roles.manage`. You can only grant permissions you hold, unless you are an owner. Reusing `x-command-id` returns the original result.

patch.description: Send the revision you last read; a newer revision returns 409. Changes apply to every member with the role on their next request. Built-in roles cannot be changed.

post.description: Reassign every member first; a role in use returns 409. Archiving revokes pending invitations for the role.

get.description: Lists up to 100 recent changes to the role and its member assignments, newest first.

get.summary: Check whether your settings command committed
Read workspace settings and your email preferences

patch.summary: Update the workspace name and display timezone

patch.description: Only workspace owners may change this mode. Observe-only preserves reads and proposals while refusing provider writes.

patch.summary: Set when approval is needed and who may approve
patch.description: Requires `workspace.approval_policy.manage`. Always requiring approval includes low-risk changes. Independent approval requires a different person; it is off while fewer than two members have access. Platform denials and required reviews still apply. Changes invalidate previous policy reviews.

get.summary: Read your Home layout and pinned pages
get.description: Layouts are personal: each member arranges their own Home and sidebar pins in each workspace. A null Home uses the default modules.

put.summary: Save your Home layout and pinned pages
put.description: Send the revision you last read. The save is rejected with 409 when another session saved a newer layout; read it again before retrying.

post.summary: Queue a test email to your account

post.description: Sending an invitation does not grant access. The invitation is bound to an active role other than Owner whose permissions you hold. An existing pending invitation must be resent or revoked; existing members cannot be invited.
Resending replaces the previous link and starts a new seven-day expiry.

get.description: Returns until when Luma support may open read-only views of this workspace, pending requests from Luma support, and inspection requests with approved inspections that are still open.

put.description: Lets Luma support open read-only views of this workspace as a member, for 24, 72 or 168 hours from now. Replaces an earlier end time. Views can’t change anything, and each one appears in Activity.

post.description: Ends support access now. Open support views end on their next request.

post.summary: Approve or decline a Luma support access request
post.description: Approving allows support access for the requested duration from now, or keeps a later end time. A request that lapsed or was answered returns 409.

post.summary: Approve or decline a Luma support inspection request
post.description: Approving lets the support team member who asked inspect this workspace’s records for thirty minutes from now. Inspection reads members, connections, sync health and access history; it can’t change anything. A request that lapsed or was answered returns 409.

post.summary: End an approved Luma support inspection
post.description: Ends approved inspection access now; the support team’s next read is refused. Emergency access can’t be revoked. Access that already ended returns 409.

post.summary: Review an invitation for your signed-in email
Accept a single-use invitation for your signed-in email
Independently read booked native receipt stock
post.description: Reads the committed entry and current balances. Repeats no posting. Later unrelated stock changes are inconclusive for the original exact quantity.

post.summary: Prepare a manual purchase receipt for native stock
post.description: Binds the current manual receipt, damage and native location ownership. Another current member approves before good units enter available and damaged units enter damaged stock. Exact retries reuse the review.

get.summary: Read native stock reviews for one purchase order

post.summary: Independently read one exact native stock source
post.description: Retains complete stock and composition evidence through Inventory. Provider observations never overwrite native balances.
Requires complete fresh stock-bearing source evidence. Another current member reviews the exact baseline before any native stock is opened.

get.summary: Read proposed stock movements and source evidence

post.description: Rechecks current source evidence, memberships and balance versions. An identical retry returns the original receipt.

post.summary: Compare independent source stock to native balances
post.description: Records source drift through virtual accounts. Provider quantities never overwrite physical native stock.

get.description: Native balances stay separate from provider observations. Unopened pools have no native opening, even when prepared zero accounts exist.

demand.description: Retained native demand for stock managers. It excludes addresses and prices and does not grant allocation authority.

post.description: Requires native order authority, reviewed location ownership and complete fresh shipment evidence. Shortages remain unallocated demand. No provider write is sent.
New verified shipments must be consumed first. A release cannot restore consumed stock. Identical retries return the original receipt.
Only exact shipment, order-line, location and unit identities consume remaining reservations. Fulfillment preparation sends no stock.
Requires fulfillment and import access. Reads one exact mapped source order, preserving complete empty reads and current mapping bindings.

get.summary: Read the exact stock ownership proposal

post.summary: Prepare a versioned location ownership step
post.description: Binds reviewed openings, current reconciliation, source mappings, account and reservation versions and workspace authority. Pending external effects prevent handover.

post.summary: Review another member’s exact ownership step
Apply an approved location ownership step
post.description: Rechecks source evidence, current reviewer grants, stock versions and authority. Activation and provider stock publication are separate controlled capabilities.

post.summary: Release due holds with fresh evidence
post.description: Processes at most 200 due holds. Stale or uncertain evidence leaves the reservation intact and returns its blocking reason.

get.description: Returns each connected mailbox with its reading state and the rules that decide which messages Luma reads. Luma reads only messages that match a rule.

put.description: Requires `messages.manage`. Fails with 409 when `expectedRevision` is not current.

post.description: Requires `messages.manage`. Luma then reads matching messages from the mailbox's backfill window. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.
Requires `messages.manage`. Luma stops reading new matching messages; threads already read stay.
Requires `messages.manage`. Schedules a read within seconds; the response does not wait for it.

get.description: Lists threads read from connected mailboxes, newest activity first unless `sort` says otherwise. `overdue` lists threads whose reply deadline passed; `review` lists threads with document facts to review. Conditions use structured thread properties only, never message text. View counts follow the search and mailbox but not the conditions.

schema.description: Threads of one mailbox. Kept for older links; prefer a `mailbox` condition.
Matches the subject or the correspondent, ignoring case.
JSON-encoded conditions: `{"match":"all"|"any","conditions":[{"field","op","value","source"}]}`. Fields and operators follow the list catalog; unsupported combinations return 400.
Group rows by a field, such as `status` or `placed:week`. Each group returns its count and its first rows.
JSON-encoded group key from `groups[].key`, such as `"open"`, `true` or `null`, to read more rows of one group. Requires `group`.
Rows returned per group, from 1 to 50.
Days, weeks and months in conditions such as `today` or `within_last`, and date groups, follow this time zone.
`activity` orders by the latest message; `due` by the reply deadline, with threads without one last in both directions.
Defaults to newest first for `activity` and earliest first for `due`.

groups.description: With `group`: each group in display order with its exact count and first rows, whose threads are in `items`. With `groupKey`: the one group, with this page of its rows.

groupsTruncated.description: More than 50 groups match; narrow the conditions to see the rest.

get.description: Returns messages with their source identity, linked records, internal notes, the thread timeline, documents and replies.

get.summary: List threads linked to a record
get.description: Requires `messages.read` and permission to read the record. Suggested links are not included.

post.description: Requires `messages.manage`. The owner must be a workspace member who can read messages. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.
Requires `messages.manage`. Null returns to the automatic deadline. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.
Requires `messages.manage`. A new inbound message reopens a closed thread. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.
Requires `messages.manage`. Notes stay in Luma and are never sent. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

post.summary: Link a thread to a record
post.description: Requires `messages.manage` and permission to read the record. Confirms a suggested link to the same record. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.
Requires `messages.manage`. Luma does not add the same automatic link again. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.
Requires `messages.manage`. Removes the text and attachment content; metadata, links and reviewed facts remain.

get.summary: Read a document and its facts
get.description: Returns the document content beside the facts proposed from it. Each fact cites its page, text span or cells.

post.description: Requires `messages.manage`. Retries a failed read; reviewed facts are kept.
Requires `messages.manage`. The locator must point to text or cells in the document. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

post.summary: Confirm, correct or reject a fact
post.description: Requires `messages.manage`. Facts that need correction cannot be confirmed unchanged. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

Requires `messages.send`. Builds the draft from the current state of the linked records and cites each one; missing or stale evidence is stated in the draft. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

put.description: Requires `messages.send`. Only drafts can change; fails with 409 when `expectedRevision` is not current.

post.summary: Send a reply or request approval
post.description: Requires `messages.send`. Replies that confirm a date or quantity, mention money, or fall under the workspace rule need approval from someone else; others are sent at once. Sending is confirmed by a fresh read of the thread.
Requires `decisions.respond` and the mailbox app’s send permission. The requester cannot approve their own reply.
Requires `messages.send`; only the requester can send. Sends at most once; repeating returns the recorded result.

post.summary: Check whether a reply was sent
post.description: Requires `messages.send`. Reads the thread again; never sends.

post.summary: Mark an uncertain supplier email as delivered or not delivered
post.description: Requires `messages.send` and `procurement.manage`. Records a person's decision after checking with the supplier; nothing is sent. `delivered` settles the email as sent; `not_delivered` as failed, so the order's submission can be drafted again. Only supplier emails in the `uncertain` state can be resolved; fails with 409 when `expectedRevision` is not current. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.
Requires `messages.send`. Only drafts and replies waiting for approval can be discarded.

get.description: Reads configured hours anchored to recorded case events. Configuration alone does not turn on automatic monitoring.

post.description: Saves a revision-checked policy. Exact command retries retain the original version. Activate Return step follow-up in Workflows to monitor automatically.

get.description: Reads owned waits, escalation and earlier occurrences without refreshing provider evidence.

post.description: Independently rereads financial evidence and records actual receipt and inspection progress. It executes no provider write.

get.description: Reads the operation, independent fulfillment and payment proof, and explicitly mapped replacement choices.

post.summary: Verify exchange consistency in both systems
post.description: Independently reads Shopify and Wawi. Completes the case only when returned stock, exactly one replacement order, its reservation, price and actual payment agree. A failed later check reopens owned work. Executes no provider write.
Freezes one native request, process, cancellation or payment hold release for independent approval. All attempts retain the same case operation. Uncertain sent writes are checked without redispatch.

post.summary: Choose how to handle replacement availability
post.description: Records wait, different item or refund with an owner. The choice does not send a provider write. A different item or refund requires independently approved and freshly verified cancellation first.

post.summary: Hand off a cancelled exchange to refund
post.description: After fresh cancellation proof, changes the proposal to refund while preserving physical inspection and restock quantities. Refunding remains a separately approved settlement.
A current independent approver responds to the frozen step. Execution uses the requester’s rechecked authority.
Resumes the same durable execution identity. A sent uncertain effect is reconciled without creating a second replacement.
Independently reads the exact native replacement, fulfillment and financial outcome. Provider acceptance does not prove payment or case closure.

get.description: Reads recorded physical and financial actions. Managers with a restock proposal also receive current Wawi warehouse choices for explicitly mapped items.

post.description: Freezes the provider-calculated refund or the inspected resale units at an explicitly mapped warehouse. Refunds never restock goods. An independent approver must authorize the exact action.
A current independent approver responds to the frozen action. Approval dispatches once as the requester after their authority and case facts are checked again.
The requester sends an approved action through Action Admission. Repeated calls do not duplicate the provider effect.
Independently reads the exact stock change or refund payment. Pending, failed and uncertain outcomes stay distinct. This command never sends a provider write.

get.description: Searches persisted return cases by case, order, source identity or item. Customer filtering also requires customers.read and follows source order mappings. No provider is called. The cursor is bound to the tenant and filters.

Requires `returns.read`. Lists the order’s return cases and, for each source of the order, how many units of every line are ordered, already in return cases or in store returns no case works, and still returnable. Each unit counts once: a store return that a case works counts only through that case.

get.description: Requires `workflows.read`. People can read saved test cases and whether each passed on the current draft revision. A case without a result has not run on this revision yet.

put.summary: Save test cases for a draft
put.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Replaces the saved test cases against the revision you loaded (0 before any are saved). If someone else saved first, the request returns 409. Retrying the same body after an uncertain response is safe.

post.summary: Run saved test cases on the current revision
post.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Runs every saved case that has no passing or running result on this draft revision. Call it after saving the draft and before publishing. Repeating the call is safe. Tests use example replies and never contact connected systems.

get.summary: Suggest example data for a test
get.description: Returns a case filled from the declared fields, cases from recent runs of the published workflow this draft edits that you can read, and scenarios from installed adapters. Nothing is saved.

post.summary: Test a draft with example data
post.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Runs the current draft revision with a saved or unsaved case. The run uses the production workflow interpreter with example replies instead of connected systems, Action Admission or action adapters. A passing test grants no activation or approval. Poll the run until it finishes. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

get.summary: Read a test run you started
get.description: Shows each step the run reached with its values, the path taken and where it would wait for a person.

post.summary: Cancel a test run you started
post.description: Stops the run, including any Code Step. Cancelling a finished run returns it unchanged.

get.description: Returns templates from installed adapters with what each needs before it can run, its readiness and its activation status here.

post.summary: Add a template to this workspace
post.description: Requires `workflows.publish`. Publishes the template’s reviewed version here so it can be configured. Repeating the request is safe. Adding a template never activates it.

get.summary: List what workflows can use in this workspace
get.description: Returns triggers, step types, subjects, data sources, actions and result checks from installed adapters. Entries that cannot run here are included with the reason.

post.summary: Check a draft without saving it
post.description: Checks a saved draft or supplied content. Diagnostics name the step and field to fix. Errors block publishing; warnings describe what cannot run in this workspace yet. Validation changes nothing.

get.description: Requires `workflows.read`. People can read drafts. Drafts never run and grant no access to connected systems.

post.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Starts a draft from scratch, from supplied content, or from a published version to edit it. Editing a published workflow never changes that version. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

put.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Saves against the revision you loaded. If someone else saved first, the request returns 409 and nothing is overwritten. Reuse the same save ID and body after an uncertain response.

post.summary: Publish a draft as a new version
post.description: Requires `workflows.publish`. Publishes the exact revision you reviewed as an immutable version. Publishing does not activate the workflow or grant it access to anything. Retrying the same revision returns the same version.
Requires `workflows.author`. Discards a draft you no longer need. Discarding again is safe. Published drafts are kept.

get.summary: Discover recurring verified work for review
get.description: Requires `workflows.author` and `issues.manage`. On an explicit request, groups at most 500 verified issues from the last 30 days by pattern, immutable resolution artifact and recorded environment. Counts describe retained human involvement and recurrence. Select evidence to request a separate proposal; discovery never invokes a model, changes a workflow or grants publication or activation authority. Returns 404 when discovery is unavailable, or 503 when the bounded cohort is too large.

get.summary: Check whether workflows can be described here
get.description: Requires `workflows.read`. Describing workflows needs a regional model route with zero data retention. When none is configured, `reason` explains what an administrator must set up.

post.summary: Start a draft from a description
post.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Describe what should happen and get a new draft with an explanation of each step, the assumptions made and open questions. Each question names the step and field to fill in. The draft uses only what this workspace has installed and still needs review, testing and publishing: generation never publishes, activates, approves or starts a workflow. The model may be asked up to three times; remaining problems are returned as diagnostics. If the model fails, times out or returns nothing usable, the request returns 503, no draft is created, and you can try again. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

post.summary: Propose a change from an instruction
post.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Describe a change to the revision you loaded. The response is a proposal with step-level changes; the draft is unchanged until the proposal is accepted. Returns 409 if the draft changed since you loaded it, and 503 with nothing changed if the model fails or times out. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

Requires `workflows.author`. Saves the proposed content as a new draft revision. If the draft changed after the proposal was made, the request returns 409 and nothing is applied. Accepting never publishes. Reuse the same save ID after an uncertain response.
Requires `workflows.author`. Discards a proposal. The draft is unchanged. Rejecting again is safe.

post.summary: Suggest a Code Step from a description
post.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Describe a calculation and get TypeScript source, returned fields, grants and example cases for the Code Step editor. The source uses only values available at that step and requests only the reads and actions directly after it. Nothing is saved. Returns 503 with nothing changed if the model fails or times out. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

get.summary: List how a draft was generated
get.description: Requires `workflows.read`. People can read the model route, token usage, attempts and outcome of each request for this draft, newest first. Prompts are stored only as a hash. These records show authorship; they don’t approve anything.

post.description: Adds a subscription revision. Historical runs retain their exact subscription and immutable workflow version. Starts must review the current subscription revision.
Records the assignee’s answer and evidence once. Answers are workflow input; provider changes still require policy admission.
Persists immutable event evidence within this workspace. Retry the exact source and body. Waiting workflows read this evidence durably.

Requires `workflows.author`. Tests an exact version with example inputs, capability replies and expected outputs. Evaluation does not call connected systems. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

post.summary: Cancel a running Code Step evaluation

post.description: Stops computation and prevents new capability requests. Actions already admitted may still complete and require reconciliation.

get.summary: Read replenishment rules and a page of stock choices
get.description: Returns up to 50 stock choices. Search by SKU or filter to a position or connection. Continue with nextCursor and the same filters. Rule readiness includes the current stock for every configured rule, independently of this page.

post.description: Requires `procurement.manage`. Reviews a stock position, supplier and quantity limits. Target stock must exceed the minimum. Reuse the exact ID and body when retrying.

Requires `procurement.manage`. Checks up to 25 stock positions before activating rules. Each position shows current stock, whether an active rule already covers it, what the first check would propose and who approves. Nothing changes.

Requires `procurement.manage`. Activates up to 25 reviewed rules, each for exactly one stock position. Each rule succeeds or fails on its own; an existing rule is never replaced. Resend the same items to retry: activated rules are returned unchanged and never duplicated.

get.summary: Read workflow coverage for a record
get.description: Returns the workflows that can cover a stock position, with the same readiness, blockers and next action as the workflow itself, scoped to that record.

post.summary: Check low stock and start replenishment
post.description: Reads current stock on the server and starts the activated version when stock is below its minimum. Reuse the request ID after an uncertain response.

get.description: Returns recorded stock, supplier, policy decision, current purchase-order status and independent verification. Responding to a pending proposal requires `procurement.manage` and `decisions.respond` and follows the workspace independent approval setting.

post.summary: Approve or reject a replenishment proposal
post.description: Requires `procurement.manage` and `decisions.respond`. The approver decides on the exact proposal under the workspace independent approval setting. Current stock, activation and policy are checked again before creating the order.

get.description: Requires `workflows.read`. People can inspect published versions and activation status. Viewing a workflow never activates it.
Read published steps, versions, prerequisites and historical grants. Process versions show the exact order of decisions, actions, waits and verification.

Returns the 50 most recent runs with subject, actor, trigger and step evidence, and the names of the people who started them. Process runs show their current state and recorded outputs. Execution and verification results are separate.

post.summary: Start or schedule a workflow run
post.description: Requires `workflows.triggers.manage`. Submits typed signal evidence for an exact version and resource. Reuse the source ID and complete body on retry. Starts do not grant execution authority. Schedules start once at the time specified by the version.

post.summary: Cancel a scheduled start or open workflow handoff

post.description: Requires `playbooks.activate`. Activates supported Resolution versions for your own principal and explicit orders on one connection. Other definitions remain available for review. Review the exact digest, scope and approval behavior. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response. Conflicting, overlapping or stale grants return 409; revoked records cannot be restored.

Requires `workflows.publish`. Lets a built-in workflow start a run for each new case of its issue type. Runs act as the caller; every change still needs policy approval under the workspace rules. Review the exact version digest and policy version. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response. A second active activation returns 409.

Requires `playbooks.activate` or `procurement.manage`. Prevents future admission under this artifact. Repeated revocation is safe. Revocation preserves historical grants and does not undo already-dispatched work.

get.summary: Check whether the API is running
Check whether the API is ready to serve requests
get.description: Returns 200 when ready and 503 when temporarily unavailable.

Authenticated SSE emits resync events with a current progress snapshot every five seconds. Refetch case, review and timeline on each event and reconnect. Last-Event-ID always resynchronizes current state; events are not an audit replay. Sessions and membership are checked before each snapshot. Streams reconnect after one minute. Slow consumers are disconnected. Use the timeline endpoint for persisted history.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Reconnects with a fresh authoritative snapshot.

200.description: SSE resync events. Refetch the subscribed resource when refetch is true.

get.description: Authenticated SSE tells workspace members which areas of data changed. Subscribe before the first query. On resync events with refetch: true, read again the views that depend on a listed topic; on reconnect, read all of them. Topics are limited to areas the member can read; decisions is available to every member. Events contain no records, totals or replay history. Last-Event-ID requests current state. Access is rechecked at least every five seconds and the stream closes when it is lost. Slow consumers disconnect and must resynchronize. Reconciliation lists every readable topic every 30 seconds.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Reconnects with a fresh authoritative snapshot.
